name: Losene Keita
summary: Guinea-born, Belgium-based former Oktagon featherweight and lightweight champion (17-2, 1-1 UFC), a patient power puncher with 11 KO/TKO wins. Lost a razor-close split decision to Nathaniel Wood on debut, then flattened Muhammad Naimov in 2:54 at UFC Paris. Takes Aaron Pico on about five weeks' notice after Arnold Allen withdrew.

how_they_fight.Striking: Counter-first power puncher: prefers to let opponents lead, then throws clubbing right hands over the top. Against Naimov he dropped him with a jab, then waited for Naimov's jab and countered with the finishing right; also caught a kick and went to the body. Lower volume (about 3.4 significant strikes a minute) and selective.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Mostly a striker; light takedown use (about 0.7 per 15 minutes). Can finish with ground strikes: retook the Oktagon lightweight belt from Ronald Paradeiser with ground-and-pound. Takedown defense untested by an elite wrestler in the UFC.
how_they_fight.Defense: Good striking defense on paper (about 66%), but Wood's calf kicks buckled him in R2 and chipped him through R3, and he was out-landed 67 to 52. Stopped once in 19 fights (Mate Sanikidze, R1 KO, 2023).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Has gone five rounds twice (UD over Paradeiser; KO of Jakub Tichota in R4). Finishes: 6 in R1, 3 in R2, 1 in R3, 1 in R4; 6 decision wins. Slow-to-moderate starter who builds into fights: his best round vs Wood was R2 and he finished with more urgency in R3, but low output can cost him close rounds.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Composed and patient, comfortable waiting for the counter; the downside is that he can cede the volume battle on the cards, as in the split loss to Wood.

patterns: Counter right hand over the top of the opponent's jab
Builds pressure, pins to the cage, then goes to the body
Finishes spread across rounds (6 R1, 3 R2, 1 R3, 1 R4)
Lower-volume, power-first approach that can lose close rounds
concerns: Weight: missed by 3 lb on three weeks' notice for his original UFC debut vs Patricio Pitbull (Sept 2025); fight cancelled
Again on a short-ish turnaround (accepted ~5 weeks out, about two weeks after his Sept. 5 fight)
Leg kicks buckled him vs Wood
Never faced a high-level wrestler like Pico in the UFC
keys_to_beat: Out-volume him and attack the lead leg
Don't lead with lazy jabs into his counter right
Mix in takedowns to make him carry weight and reduce his power shots

news.text: Made weight at the official weigh-ins: 146 lb (Pico 145.5). No repeat of his 2025 UFC Paris miss.
Media day: says he asked for any Abu Dhabi fight, that every shot he throws is meant to hurt Pico, and that he is the better martial artist.
Sherdog preview: -105 (Pico -115); picks him by first-round KO, expecting Pico's defensive lapses to resurface.
UFC.com Fight By Fight Preview: back about seven weeks after his Paris KO of Naimov.
Replaces injured Arnold Allen against Aaron Pico at UFC 333; posted video accepting on short notice.
KO'd Muhammad Naimov at 2:54 of R1 at UFC Paris (first UFC win), then hopped the cage to sit cageside; called the win a 'warning shot' to Lerone Murphy.
Missed weight by 3 lb (149) for his scheduled debut vs Patricio Pitbull at UFC Paris; bout cancelled.
